bib.title: Multi-agent Architecture Search via Agentic Supernet
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 267, 2025

question: Can automated multi-agent system design be made query-dependent, by optimising a distribution over architectures instead of one static system, to cut inference cost while keeping or raising accuracy?
hypothesis: A one-size-fits-all searched workflow wastes resources on easy queries and fails across domains; a sampled, query-conditioned architecture from a supernet should be cheaper and at least as accurate.
contributions: Paradigm reformulation: agentic supernet, a probabilistic continuous distribution over agentic architectures
MaAS framework that evolves and adaptively allocates resource-efficient solutions per query
Evaluation on six benchmarks: 0.54-16.89% higher performance, lower training/inference cost, cross-benchmark and cross-LLM transfer, inductive capacity

method.summary: An L-layer agentic supernet holds a per-layer probability over agentic operators (CoT, Debate, Self-Consistency, Self-Refine, Ensemble, Testing, ReAct, early exit). A MoE-style controller conditioned on the query embedding selects operators layer by layer until a cumulative score threshold; the sampled DAG executes. The layer distribution is updated by a cost-aware Monte Carlo gradient estimate and the operators (prompts, temperature, structure) by LLM-generated textual gradients.
method.task: Automated multi-agent workflow search for math reasoning, code generation and tool use (GAIA)

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.size: 617 level-5 problems from 4 types (119 train / 486 test)
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2021; subset following Hong et al. 2024

other.note: Table 7 labels it Qwen-2.5-70b in the MATH block

models.name: MaAS controller Qϕ
models.architecture: MoE-style network with FFN scoring over concatenated embeddings of query and previous-layer operators

other.embedding: MiniLM (Wang et al. 2020) over LLM-written operator profiles; Sentence-Bert also mentioned

training.objective: min E[-p(a|q,π,O) + λ·C(G;q)]; π gradient by Monte Carlo with cost-aware importance weights m_k (Eq 11); operators by textual gradient (Eq 12)

other.lambda: {1e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2}; value used per benchmark not stated
other.population_N: Fig 7 also varies population size N, not defined in text

inference.samples: inferred: one sampled architecture per query; number of runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Operator prompts evolved by textual gradient; no fixed prompt

parameters.operators: CoT; LLM-Debate (3 debaters, up to 2 rounds); Self-Consistency (5 CoT, majority vote); Self-Refine (max 5 iterations); Ensemble (3 LLM agents, pairwise ranking); Testing; ReAct; Early exit

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction correct on GSM8K, MATH, MultiArith, GAIA

metrics.name: Cost
metrics.definition: Token count, API USD, wall-clock minutes (Table 3); per-query cost in 10^-3 $ (Table 4)

eval.protocol: All baselines on gpt-4o-mini; no seeds, repeats or significance tests stated. AFlow restricted to gpt-4o-mini, MAX_ITERATION=20; AgentSquare early stopping patience 5.

prompts.text: You are an expert machine learning researcher specializing in designing agentic systems. Your objective is to create building blocks such as prompts and control flows within these systems to solve complex tasks.

limits: Optimizer, learning rate, epochs, batch size, hardware and seeds for training the controller are not given.
Train sets are tiny (33-264 queries) and no seeds or variance are reported, so differences of about 0.5 points are not testable.
Which lambda was used per benchmark is not stated; Table 4 costs (10^-3 $) and Table 3 inference cost are not reconciled.
Sensitivity of 'population size N' in Fig 7 is not described in text.
Baselines are re-run on gpt-4o-mini only; MaAS tuned per benchmark, GAIA train set only 94 tasks.
Authors state no ethical concerns; no failure analysis offered.

terms.definition: A composite LLM-agent invocation process that involves multiple LLM calls and tool usage
A probabilistic, continuous agentic architecture distribution encompassing many possible multi-agent candidates, as an L-layer cascade with per-layer operator probabilities
Agent-generated textual analyses used to update prompt, temperature and operator node structure
